status: Secondary diagnostic designed after inspecting orthogonal-code aggregate results; not a prespecified primary test.
reason: The separable control knows the true encoder and removes observation noise perpendicular to its span. Compare a projection-matched natural network to distinguish that information advantage from cross-latent interactions. Also quantify effects of the known [0,1] target bounds.
networks: all 60 networks per family, both fixed endpoints; no selection by p or recovery
data: Reuse exactly the already sealed recovery examples, contexts and Gaussian draws at std 0/0.15/0.35/0.6
methods: natural after known-context orthogonal projection onto the encoder column span
projection: P_B=B*(B^T B)^-1*B^T; context left unchanged. Natural and separable now receive the same known-subspace filtering. This is oracle preprocessing, not a learned correction stage.
geometry_invariance: For feature-axis perturbations of clean encoded inputs, projection leaves the input unchanged. Verify projected/natural outputs agree on the entire first-pair 31x31 absent ++ grid at each context. Thus projection changes recovery to isotropic observation noise while preserving the primary feature-plane geometry.
metrics: clean MSE and its increase under corruption
scope: Do not claim output clipping preserves geometry. Do not infer a specific learned correction mechanism from a raw-versus-projected difference. The projection uses ground-truth generative information supplied to the analytic controls. No new training or model selection.
